contexts.text: What is the prayer of the mouth, if the mind is not in it, but babbling?
(Why the Lord prayed to the Father.)
He shall pray for thee () = it will thus be revealed.

Prayer, regarded in itself, is talking with God; and some internal view then of the matters of the prayer, to which there answers something like an influx into the perception or thought of the mind, so that there is a certain opening of the man's interiors towards God; but this with a difference according to the man's state, and according to the essence of the Thing which is [the subject] of the prayer. If [it is] from love and faith, and if it is only celestial and spiritual things, concerning which and for which, he prays, there then comes forth in the prayer a something like revelation, which is manifested in the affection of him who is praying, as to hope, comfort, or a certain internal joy. Hence it is that to pray, in the internal sense, = to be revealed. Still more here, (because) by the prophet is meant the Lord, whose prayer was nothing else than internal speech with the Divine, and at the same time revelation. Illustrated.
Abraham prayed to God () = revelation. (Explained.)

Isaac prayed to Jehovah () = the communication of the Divine which is the Son with the Divine which is the Father. To pray = to be communicated; for prayer is nothing but communication... This communication was in the Lord... AC 3291.
Pray for those who injure and persecute you. Explained.
For in prayer from the Divine it is always thought and believed that the Lord alone knows whether it is conducive or not...
(They think) that the Lord continually prays to the Father...
It has been granted to perceive the influx itself... the application to the objects of the prayer...
In His state of humiliation He prayed to the Father as to another...
Who does not see God before him... while he is praying?.
In the exhortation before the Holy Communion. TCR 722:3. TCR 812.
I saw a company of Spirits on their knees praying to God to send Angels...
It is general in all Divine worship for man first to want, long for, and pray; and the Lord then answers, informs, and does: otherwise the man does not receive anything Divine. Illustrated.
Who thinks otherwise... who prays from this formula... Does he not pray to God the Father as one God... (Thus) he makes the three Persons three Gods, when he thus prays. BE 35:2. TCR 623:2.
That (doctrinal truth in the Word) can be seen by those who pray to God the Father (shown to be impossible). AR 566:2.
We will pray to the Lord to let us ascend (from the abyss). And, as they prayed to the Lord, leave was granted.
Had taught that they should pray to the Father for the sake of the Son...
I prayed to the Lord, and suddenly the interiors of my mind were opened...

That he who knows anything about the Lord's Advent, and the New Heaven and the New Church... should pray that it may come; and that he who longs for truths, should pray that the Lord may come with light; and he who loves truths will then receive them from the Lord without any labour of his own. Signified, Explained.
To the sermon he subjoined a votive prayer...
He threw himself on his knees, and prayed devoutly to the Lord to be instructed. And then an Angel appeared...
If you should pray at home and at church a thousand times that...
Ae have prayed from our faith that...
Hence it is that the Lord prayed to the Father that He might do His will.

Henceforth no one in Christian lands who does not believe in the Lord is heard; his prayers, in Heaven, are like bad smelling odours, and like eructations from diseased lungs; and, although he may suppose that his prayer is like incense... it ascends into the angelic Heaven just as the smoke of a conflagration, which, driven downwards by a tempest, is thrown back into his eyes...
He had confirmed himself... by the fact that the Son prayed to the Father...
That in the world the Lord prayed to the Father was according to the order established from creation. Explained.

This prayer has been commanded for this time, to wit, that God the Father be approached through His Human... This is the true explication of the words of that prayer. (Namely, Our Father...) TCR 113:5.
The Angels said to me, We will pray to the Lord to allow us to descend...
Then the instructive and prayer-like preaching in the temples is... borne into the heart... (See also TCR 798:8.)
That the revengeful can pray devoutly. Explained.
As to their prayer to the Lord... they had only a verbal or literal sense of the prayer...

When I was in prayer, such a thought was insinuated into the sense of the prayer; namely, that a crowd of many things inflowed into the ideas of the thought and prayer, and therefore the ideas are unordinated...
In infancy I wanted to hold my breath while they were praying... (Compare SE 3464:2.)
When angelic Spirits wanted to pray from me...
A certain prayer was uttered by a woman... women can enunciate with affection, and thus excite to devotion... But it is rarely that such are interiorly devout. Example(s).

He prayed to the Father, and an answer was given in various ways by a certain Spirit; but after his prayers he always acquired for himself confederacies, and went with them to destroy me... SE 5977. LJPost 245.
They besought me not to say to them the words in the exhortation before the Communion...
To pray all the time () = to prepare themselves.

To ask, and pray () = the life of love and charity; for to those in (this) life the Lord gives what to ask for; and therefore they ask for nothing but what is good; and this is done to them... and, as the prayers proceed from the life of charity, and are according to it... it is added, when ye stand praying forgive...
That when ye stand praying = when they are in Divine worship. Illustrated.
To pray for him continually () = that they will be continually withheld from falsities, and kept in truths. AE 329:18.
To pray (for those who persecute us) = intercession. Explained.

To pray, in the universal sense, = all the truth which man thinks and speaks... Those who do good and speak truth (for their own sakes) are meant by those who do alms, and pray, in secret; for they do and pray from the love or affection, thus from the Lord...
(A prayer given.)
(Luther) prayed to the Lord that he might recede from his falsities...
The English were praised on account of that exhortation... but many of them said that it is for the common people... LJPost 285.
These preachers are loved by the citizens (of London); they speak in accordance with the exhortation... LJPost 297.
